correctness.rationale: All real-order cases are reconstructed: H_alpha is a second-difference generating function. Two convergent fractional-power Laplace representations and sharp Möbius disk bounds yield inf 0 for 0<alpha<1 and 4eta(-alpha)>0 for 1<alpha<2. Integer cases are rational identities. A fixed-sector complex Riemann-sum asymptotic makes real parts unbounded below for alpha>2. Eta signs and repeated Rolle prove a negative-real zero for all alpha>2. Numeric checker tests finite sample cases only; proof is analytic.

originality.rationale: The exact sharp real-part infimum for every alpha>=0, with its jump at alpha=1, eta(-alpha) floor for 1<alpha<2, and negative-infinite regime for alpha>2, was compared as a statement and not merely a title. Wood (1992) already discusses polylog zeros; their qualitative existence/absence is credited and is not the originality basis. Full accessible sections of Bénéteau et al. and Savage-Visontai have distinct objects or scopes. The older Fornberg-Kolbig full text was inaccessible and is recorded as risk.
residual_risks: The full primary 1975 Fornberg–Kölbig paper was not accessible; an unexpectedly equivalent sharp real-part inequality could exist there or in older geometric-function theory.
The exact first public day of the Wood 1992 report is unverified; it is cited only as older mathematical background, not used to manufacture a day-precise source date.

value.rationale: This identifies the best real-part lower bound of the normalized full Bergman-type reproducing kernel over the entire open disk at every nonnegative real weight exponent. The discontinuous floor at alpha=1, sharp positive eta lower bound for 1<alpha<2, switch in the extremal boundary point, and failure by negative blow-up beyond two give a natural complete analytic invariant stronger than the classical zero count; the resulting uniform kernel lower bounds are useful for quantitative estimates.
